title: Tag Registry Label Retirement Delivery
summary: remove the redundant label field from canonical tag registry rows and make every consumer display the flat tag_id directly
content_html:
Tag Registry Label Retirement Delivery

Target Result

tag_id is both canonical identity and the displayed tag name. Canonical registry rows no longer store a duplicate label.

{
  "tag_id": "moss",
  "group": "subject",
  "description": "<temporary document seed content>",
  "updated_at_utc": "<timestamp>"
}

The cutover input had 245 registry rows. All 245 labels were identical to their tag_id, so retirement requires no naming decision, identity rewrite, alias migration, or assignment migration.

In Scope

  • Remove label from every canonical registry row and bump the registry schema to tag_registry_v3.
  • Preserve every tag_id, scalar group, description, row timestamp, policy, alias target, and assignment reference.
  • Stop create, edit, promotion, and manual-patch paths from writing label.
  • Stop validation and mutation evidence from requiring or returning a registry label where tag_id already carries the same value.
  • Make Tag Registry, Tag Aliases, Series Tags, and Series Tag Editor consume and display tag_id directly.
  • Update focused fixtures, planners, APIs, browser modules, validation, checks, and durable source documentation.

Not In Scope

  • Renaming a tag or changing any tag identity.
  • Changing group membership, descriptions, aliases, assignments, weights, or inheritance.
  • Removing generic UI or configuration fields named label when they do not represent tag_registry.tags[*].label.
  • Adding doc_id, creating tag documents, or removing registry descriptions.
  • Changing the group taxonomy or group-derived reporting.

Delivery Steps

  1. [x] Freeze and validate the input. Require tag_registry_v2, exactly one allowed scalar group per tag, globally unique flat IDs, and label === tag_id for every row. Record tag, alias-target, and assignment-reference counts before changing source.
  2. [x] Change the canonical contract. Add tag_registry_v3 validation and a one-file projection that removes only label. Preserve tag order, policy, groups, descriptions, and row timestamps; update only the source-level version and cutover timestamp.
  3. [x] Update every writer. Remove label from create, edit, promotion, API response, activity detail, state projection, and manual-patch behavior. Ensure ordinary group/description edits cannot reintroduce the field.
  4. [x] Update every reader. Remove raw-label requirements and use tag_id for registry display, search, ordering, alias target choices, Series Tags, and Series Tag Editor suggestions/chips. Keep generic presentation labels only where they are derived values rather than canonical source.
  5. [x] Cut over once. Apply the validated v2-to-v3 registry projection atomically. Do not add a dual-read source mode or retain empty/derived label compatibility fields.
  6. [x] Reconcile and close. Prove 245 IDs, groups, descriptions, and row timestamps are preserved; aliases and assignments are byte-unchanged and still resolve; no registry row contains label; and no writer recreates it. Run focused model/planner/API tests, studio-tag-smoke, scoped source searches, and manual Registry/Aliases/Series Tags/Series Tag Editor checks.

Likely Authority

  • studio/data/canonical/tags/tag-registry.json
  • studio/services/tags/tag_source_model.py
  • studio/services/tags/tag_registry_mutations.py
  • studio/services/tags/tag_promotion_mutations.py
  • studio/services/tags/tag_flat_identity_migration.py
  • studio/app/server/studio/studio_tag_api/
  • studio/app/frontend/js/studio-tag-data.js
  • studio/app/frontend/js/tag-registry-*
  • studio/app/frontend/js/tag-aliases-*
  • studio/app/frontend/js/series-tags-*
  • studio/app/frontend/js/analytics-tag-*
  • focused tag fixtures, planner/API tests, and Studio tag smokes

These are inspection starting points. The exact implementation should change only consumers of the canonical registry label field.

Completion Evidence

  • The guarded projection removed 245 labels and preserved 245 IDs, scalar groups, descriptions, and row timestamps in their existing order. Current validation reports 245 tags, 70 aliases, 71 alias targets, and 8 assignment references.
  • tag-registry.json is tag_registry_v3; all 245 rows omit label. Its post-cutover SHA-256 is 184cb1654608f02214bacb0d6d727cb35bb3136ad1ce41589dae97f67f8c26ed.
  • Alias and assignment bytes did not change. Their pre/post SHA-256 values are 9bdcd5ac7df75719ba791480ff45612137ce1832e5c0595eaf8e23a376701158 and 08c0dba8bf923be376f1b8186290a00b1a2bdb7c74ad811f896eb1f430b72d5d.
  • Focused model/planner/API tests pass 53/53. The maintained studio-tag-smoke profile passes 11/11 in var/admin/test-runs/tag-registry-label-retirement-rerun/.
  • Scoped runtime searches find no raw registry-label reader and no browser or server registry-label writer. Derived presentation objects may still use a generic label key populated from tag_id.
  • Manual local-browser checks showed 245 flat IDs in Tag Registry, the selected group and a transient alternative selection in the simplified Edit Tag modal, 70 aliases with flat targets, Series Tags chips for series 036, and flat-ID suggestions and assignment chips in Series Tag Editor. No save was performed during manual validation.

Durable Destinations

Update Tag Source Data, Tag Registry, and Series Tags with the shipped schema and display contract.

Flat Tag Identity Concept continues to own the identity/group model. This delivery owns only retirement of the duplicate registry field.
